title: Almighty (CCC 268–278)
hook: God shows his almighty power most of all in mercy

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Creed's shape: Father, Son and Spirit. Your line was three movements. Today, one word from the Creed's first line.

What does strength look like? A weightlifter with the bar overhead. A storm that peels a roof off. A fist on a table. Now another scene: a big man down on one knee on a sidewalk, tying a toddler's shoe, careful not to pull the laces too tight. That's strength too, the kind that holds itself back. The Creed calls God the Father almighty, and when the Catechism explains that word, it makes a claim about where that power shows most. Today's word: almighty.
screen: `A WEIGHTLIFTER. A STORM. A FIST.` → `A MAN TYING A TODDLER'S SHOE.` → `WHERE DOES POWER SHOW MOST?`

segments.voice: Almighty means able to do all things. Mary sings it in Luke's Gospel, in the Douay-Rheims: "he that is mighty, hath done great things to me." But the Book of Wisdom ties that power to something unexpected, saying to God: "thou hast mercy upon all, because thou canst do all things." Mercy because of power, not in spite of it. The Catechism pairs the Creed's two words, Father and almighty, and says they shed light on each other: a father's power, never arbitrary, never a whim. Then it faces the hard question that day two hundred ninety-nine called why evil. If God is almighty, why so much suffering? The Catechism admits that faith in God's power can be put to the test by evil. Its answer points to the cross, where God looks weakest; Paul calls the crucified Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God. The Catechism says God shows his almighty power by turning people from their sins and bringing them back to friendship with him. And it quotes a prayer of the Roman Mass that goes further: God shows his almighty power most of all by sparing and by showing mercy. On this reading, any force can break things; it takes a deeper power to forgive, and to heal what's broken. The Creed's first adjective isn't a threat hanging over the world. It's the strength of someone who can afford to be gentle.
screen: `MERCY UPON ALL, FOR THOU CANST DO ALL.` · `FATHER AND ALMIGHTY TOGETHER.` · `THE CROSS: THE POWER OF GOD.` · `POWER SHOWN MOST IN MERCY.`

segments.voice: Think of a moment coming up today when you'll hold a little power: over a child, a coworker who made a mistake, someone on a customer service line, a slow driver ahead of you. Picture it clearly, then picture using that power gently, a softer word, a little patience, a small offense let go, and rehearse it once, start to finish. If you pray, ask God for that kind of strength; if you don't, just hold the picture steady.
Almighty. Able to do all things, and, in the Catechism's reading, showing that power above all in mercy and forgiveness. Today's word.
Your line: power as mercy. Like a big man kneeling to tie a small shoe. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics profess God as the Father almighty in the Creed at Mass, and some of the Church's prayers, including the one the Catechism quotes, address God's power and his mercy together.

fork.setup: the Catechism quotes a prayer of the Mass on how God shows his almighty power most of all. what does it say?
fork.reveal: most of all by sparing and showing mercy. the Catechism adds that God shows his power by turning people from their sins and back to friendship with him.

chat.says: What does almighty even mean? Sounds like God just smashes whatever he wants.
options: The Catechism says it's a father's power, never a whim, and it shows most in mercy and forgiving.
It means God's power works by fear: the Creed puts it first so that people will obey.
It means God can do anything except forgive, since mercy would make him look weak.
chat.meaning: The Catechism pairs Father and almighty: a power never arbitrary. A Mass prayer it quotes says God shows his almighty power most of all by sparing and showing mercy.

notes: Confirm Challoner wording of Luke 1:49 and Wisdom 11:24 (Challoner verse numbering).

Catechism paraphrased (copyright): fatherhood and power shed light on each other (CCC 270); power never arbitrary (CCC 271); faith tested by evil, the cross as God's power (CCC 272); power shown above all in forgiving sins and restoring friendship, with the collect (CCC 277). Confirm.
The Missal collect (Latin 'Deus, qui omnipotentiam tuam parcendo maxime et miserando manifestas') is paraphrased in English from the Latin; the current English Missal text is copyrighted.
Hook: 'it makes a claim about where that power shows most' rests on the index hook ('most of all in mercy'), which follows the collect.
Review: 'one word from the Creed's first line' (Father almighty); confirm it reads well for both creeds.
Original: παντοκράτωρ as the Greek creeds' word for almighty; confirm.

Editor: 'above all' / 'most of all' now attributed only to the Missal collect, which says it; CCC 277's own sentence says God shows his power by converting us and restoring friendship (teach and fork). howItsDone's 'often' softened.
